Synopsis:
The US military, under SouthCom, has conducted lethal strikes against vessels allegedly involved in narco-trafficking in the Eastern Pacific, bringing the total to 223 killed across 67 strikes since September. The campaign's effectiveness is heavily questioned — drug flows are largely unaffected, fentanyl primarily enters via land from Mexico, and investigations have identified victims who were likely civilian fishers. The Trump administration is simultaneously negotiating land-based joint military operations in Colombia, Guatemala, Honduras, and Ecuador. Legal challenges, UN condemnation, and a Pentagon IG review are ongoing.
